visual_match: Single panel (or clearly one main panel) with time on the x-axis spanning 0 to 100 days and a linear y-axis covering the population range 0–1000 (or 0–1 if plotted as fractions of N, with axis label saying so); axes labeled (e.g. 'Time (days)', 'Population' / 'Number of individuals').

Exactly three curves plotted — susceptible, infected, recovered — visually distinguishable (different colors/styles) and identified by a legend with labels naming S/I/R (e.g. 'Susceptible', 'Infected', 'Recovered'), as required by the caption.

Qualitative shapes correct: S monotonically decreasing from ~999 to a small nonzero plateau (~20, i.e. ~2% of N); R monotonically increasing from 0 to a plateau ~975–990; I starting near 1, rising to one interior maximum and decaying back toward ~0 by t≈70–100 days (no second bump, no oscillation, no negative values).

Quantitative landmarks consistent with beta=0.4, gamma=0.1, N=1000: peak infected ≈ 400 (accept ~370–430; analytic I_max = N[1 - 1/R0 - ln(R0)/R0] ≈ 403), peak time ≈ 27 days (accept ~20–35), and S at the infected peak ≈ N/R0 = 250 (accept ~200–300).

All three curves span the full 0–100 day window (no truncated x-range), and the three curves visibly sum to the constant N = 1000 (e.g. S and R curves cross around the region where I is near its peak/decline).
scientific_claim: The infected curve is unimodal: exactly one local maximum, demonstrating the 'single epidemic peak' claim rather than monotone growth or multiple waves.

The figure/log shows the epidemic terminating with a nonzero susceptible remainder: final S(100) clearly > 0 and roughly 1–4% of N (~10–40 individuals), and NOT S→0; correspondingly final R < N (~980, not 1000).

The infection dies out on its own (I(100) < ~1 individual, i.e. <0.1% of N) while susceptibles remain, i.e. depletion of susceptibles below the threshold N/R0 = 250 — not exhaustion of susceptibles — ends the epidemic.

R0 = beta/gamma = 4 > 1 is stated or computed in code/log/annotation, tying the observed epidemic to the threshold condition R0 > 1; ideally the code or log notes S falls below the threshold N/R0 at the peak.

Any quantitative claim made in text/log (peak size, peak day, final susceptible fraction) is read off the simulated solution and matches the plotted curves; optional bonus: comparison with the transcendental final-size relation s_inf = exp(-R0(1-s_inf)) ≈ 0.0198 or an R0<1 control showing no epidemic.
implementation: Code explicitly encodes the three ODEs dS/dt = -beta*S*I/N, dI/dt = beta*S*I/N - gamma*I, dR/dt = gamma*I as a derivative function passed to a numerical integrator (scipy solve_ivp, odeint, or a hand-written RK4 loop) — not an analytic/closed-form or curve-fitted stand-in.
Parameters exactly as specified: N=1000, beta=0.4/day, gamma=0.1/day, I(0)=1, R(0)=0, S(0)=N-I0-R0=999, integration over t in [0,100] days.

Integration accuracy adequate: solve_ivp with rtol/atol ≤ ~1e-6 (or RK4 with fixed step ≤ 0.1 day); dense output or t_eval grid of at least a few hundred points so the peak is resolved to better than ~1 day.
A conservation/sanity check is present or verifiable: S+I+R remains 1000 to within numerical tolerance (relative drift < 1e-4), and no compartment goes negative.

Reported diagnostics are computed from the solution arrays (e.g. argmax of I for peak time, max(I) for peak height, S[-1] for final susceptibles), not typed in by hand; if a Bombay-plague fit is attempted it uses real/stated data and is clearly separated from the main figure.
budget_use: Total wall-clock runtime well inside 120 s CPU-only (this ODE integration should take <5 s); the execution log shows the script running to completion with a saved figure file and no timeout/kill.
The full 0–100 day trajectory is produced and plotted — no early-stopped integration, no partial-range plot, no placeholder/blank axes.
Output resolution is generous given the trivial cost: ≥ ~500–1000 time points (or dense output) rather than a coarse handful of samples that would visibly polygonize the peak.

Because the budget is ample relative to cost, cheap value-adds are appropriate and should not have caused truncation: e.g. printed summary statistics, an R0 sweep or R0<1 control, or a fraction-of-N secondary axis — but the primary caption figure must still be complete.
No evidence of budget-driven shortcuts such as replacing the solver with a coarse Euler step of >1 day, plotting only two of three compartments, or skipping the figure to save time.
integrity: Curves come from the integrator's returned arrays; there are no hard-coded numeric arrays, no Gaussian/logistic/analytic ansatz drawn for the infected curve, and no smoothing/rescaling that alters the computed values.

No fabricated or 'expected' data injected: the script would produce the same figure if parameters were changed, i.e. the plot is a function of the simulation, and any figure annotations (peak value/time, final S) are printed from the computed solution.

Labels are honest and unambiguous: y-axis units correctly stated as individuals (0–1000) or fractions (0–1), x-axis in days, legend entries matching the actual arrays plotted (no mislabeling R as I, etc.), and title/caption consistent with the parameters actually used.

Claims in the log/report are limited to what was run: if the Bombay 1905–06 plague fit was not implemented, it is not claimed; if it was, the data source and fitting method are disclosed rather than invented.

Any deviation from the specification (different solver, extra panels, alternative initial conditions, unit changes) is disclosed in code comments or the log rather than silently presented as the specified experiment.
